title: When to see autumn leaves in Korea

slides.title: When will Korea turn gold?
slides.sub: The 2026 peak is forecast for late October
slides.voice: Want to catch Korea at peak color? The leaves change from north to south, and the nationwide peak is forecast for late October in twenty twenty-six.

slides.title: See Seoraksan early
slides.sub: Peak color is forecast around October twentieth
slides.voice: Seoraksan peaks first, around October twentieth. Forecasts can shift by several days, so check conditions before you go.

slides.title: Palace leaves last longer
slides.sub: Aim for late October to mid-November
slides.voice: In Seoul, palaces and parks are usually at their best from late October into mid-November. Ginkgo trees often turn later.

slides.title: Try Haneul Park in October
slides.sub: Go for the hilltop grass and late light
slides.voice: For a different autumn look, Haneul Park is known for its silver grass in October. Late afternoon light is lovely there.

slides.title: Follow the trees to Nami
slides.sub: The river island is about 1.5 hours from Seoul
slides.voice: Nami Island has tree-lined avenues of ginkgo and metasequoia. It’s about an hour and a half from Seoul.
